title: Jameis Winston sings ‘Who Let The Dogs Out’ to try to draw offsides penalty
content:
New York Giants backup quarterback Jameis Winston got creative when trying to draw the Washington Commanders’ defense offside in the fourth quarter of “Thursday Night Football” at MetLife Stadium.

In a fourth-and-1 attempt from the Giants’ 11-yard line, Winston went through the snap calls.

“Get ready. Get set. Hut 1, hut 2, hut 3.”

And when the Commanders didn’t budge, Winston tried a different method.

“Who let the dogs out? Who? Who? Who? Who?” Winston sang, which was picked up by the Amazon Prime microphones.

Al Michaels and Kirk Herbstreit burst into laughter in the broadcast booth.

“You got to be kidding me!” Michaels remarked.

“What is he doing?” Herbstreit said.

The Commanders didn’t bite, and the Giants took the delay-of-game penalty and punted the ball away. But even if the attempt was unsuccessful, it produced another highlight to add to the Jameis Winston experience, a mixed bag on the field but an always-entertaining one off of it.

“It just had a nice ring to it,” Winston said after the game, explaining why he chose the Baha Men classic to bark at the line of scrimmage. Winston added that he came up with the idea at practice.

The Commanders completed a 24-21 comeback win in the final minute, securing their first road victory of the season and loosening the Giants’ grip on first place in the NFC East.

Offenses have long experimented with ways to draw opponents offside in short-yardage situations to gain a first down. During a 2025 game against the Las Vegas Raiders, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes appeared to try it, before throwing his hands up in frustration when it didn’t work.

“This f—ing never f—ing works, man!” Mahomes screamed.

As it turned out, it was all an act. A few seconds later, Mahomes called for the snap, taking advantage of a Raiders defense that might have let its guard down. Mahomes handed the ball off to running back Kareem Hunt for a run that gained a first down and later joked that his acting skills must have come from “all of my State Farm commercials.”
